sample1.title: Congress Debates New Housing Act as Rents Climb
sample1.summary: Lawmakers clashed over a proposal to cap plot rents in central Redmont, with a final vote expected next week.
sample1.body:
Members of Congress spent Tuesday's session debating the proposed Housing Affordability Act, which would cap the rent charged on residential plots in central Redmont.

Supporters argue that rents have risen sharply over the past month and that new citizens are being priced out of the city centre.

## What the bill would do

The act would limit yearly rent increases and require landlords to register their plots with the Department of Commerce.

> "Every citizen deserves a place to build," said one representative during the debate.

Opponents warned that a cap could discourage new construction. A final vote is expected next week.

sample2.title: District Court Rules in Shop Dispute
sample2.summary: A magistrate found that a verbal sale agreement was not enough to override a shop owner's records.
sample2.body:
The District Court has ruled in a dispute between a shop owner and a customer who claimed a private sale had been agreed in chat.

The magistrate found that the customer could not produce any record of the agreement and ordered the items' value to be returned.

## Why it matters

The ruling is a reminder to **keep written records** of private deals, whether in a signed book or a screenshot.

sample3.title: Market Day Returns to the Capitol Plaza
sample3.summary: Traders and builders gathered for the first market day of the season, with stalls selling everything from wool to redstone.
sample3.body:
Dozens of citizens filled the Capitol Plaza on Saturday for the return of Market Day.

Stalls offered everything from dyed wool and building blocks to redstone contraptions, and several new businesses used the event to introduce themselves.

Organisers say the next market day will be held at the end of the month.
